F-b8xt: source-assisted reading, 22 September 2026.
Reader: Codex subagent; exact model identifier unavailable.
Frozen base: review-2026-09-22-image-only.json, unchanged. Exposure: the prior F-b8xt report, its Aquinas and Versor suggestions, cached cmp07.html and live Corpus Thomisticum, and expanded manuscript coverage. This is not an independent reading. The frozen crop covers the start of r.a, not the diagnostic passage near the foot of r.b; it cannot be treated as independent corroboration of the Aquinas connection.

Selected expanded reading. Parentheses mark proposed expansions of abbreviations, [?] uncertain readings, [...] unread text. Physical line references follow the column count in the existing report and were located in the full recto/crops; the printed source is not used to fill gaps. Ordinary letter forms replace some cursive signs. Crop rb5 overlaps rb6 at the line ending substantiam; rb6 overlaps rb7 at omnia alia; these are not repeated manuscript lines. No securely deciphered correction is integrated in the selected excerpts.

Recto b, lower portion, z/rb5.jpg and z/rb6.jpg:
r.b41 ubi q(ue)r(itur): q(uod)[?] si q(ue)ra(tur) quid e(st) h(om)o (et) r(espon)d(etur)
r.b42 a(n)i(m)al, li a(n)i(m)al q(uia) e(st) in g(e)n(er)e s(ubstanti)e no(n) sol(um)
r.b43 d(icit) q(ui)d e(st) h(om)o s(ed) (et)ia(m)[?] a(bsolu)te s(ignifica)t q(ui)d, i(d) e(st)
r.b44 s(ubstanti)am. S(ed) cu(m) q(ue)r(itur) q(ui)d e(st) alb(e)do (et) r(espon)d(etur)
r.b45 q(uod) e(st) color, li color li(cet) s(ignifice)t quid e(st)
r.b46 alb(e)do, t(ame)n no(n) a(bsolu)te s(ignifica)t quid s(ed) q(ua)le,
r.b47 (et) i(de)o q(ua)litas no(n) h(abe)t q(ui)d si(mpliciter) s(ed) s(ecundu)m q(ui)d
r.b48 ut color e(st) q(ui)d alicuius[?], (et) h(oc) q(ui)d magis
r.b49 p(otes)t[?] dici s(ubstanti)ale q(uam) s(ubstanti)a; q(uia) cu(m)[?]
r.b50 o(mn)ia alia p(re)dic(ament)a h(ab)e(n)t r(ati)o(n)e(m) e(nt)is a s(ubstanti)a

The particles and technical abbreviation expansions are source-assisted and remain proposals. The second li before color and the phrase potest dici at r.b49 should not be erased to agree with Aquinas. Alicuius is plausible but less secure than color and quid. The opening word of the corollary at r.b39 is visible; its full heading is not securely transcribed here.

Continuation, z/rb7.jpg and z/va1.jpg:
r.b51 [i(de)o?] [...] mod(us) e(nt)it(a)t(is) s(ubstanti)e .s. e(ss)e quid
r.b52 p(ar)ticipat(ur) s(ecundu)m q(ua)nda(m) si(mi)litudi(n)e(m) p(ro)p(or)tio(n)is
r.b53 in o(mn)ib(us) aliis p(re)dic(ament)is, ut sic(ut) a(n)i(m)al e(st)
v.a01 quid e(st) h(om)o, ita color e(st) quid e(st) al-
v.a02 bedinis (et) nu(mer)us e(st) quid e(st) dualit(a)t(is), (et)
v.a03 [...] p(ate)t p(er)[?] p(re)dicta[?] [...]

The old report left the last recto lines as an unspecified continuation. Counting through its r.b50, the three remaining physical lines are labelled r.b51–53 here. The first words of r.b51 are cramped/uncertain and not reconstructed from the edition. Aquinas has quid hominis / color albedinis / numerus dualitatis; the manuscript repeatedly writes quid est. The transition to the next corollary follows in v.a04. This further continuation strengthens the textual connection beyond the familiar man/whiteness examples.

Additional passage, verso b, z/vb1.jpg and upper-right verso tile:
v.b01 3a (con)cl(usi)o. diff(initio) (et) q[...] q[...] erat e(ss)e q(uid)ditative[?] su(n)t
v.b02 (et) p(ro)p(ri)e solis sp(ecie)b(us) sp(ecialissi)mis de g(e)n(er)e
v.b03 s(ubstanti)e. p(ate)t p(ri)m(o) p(er) p(hilosophu)m in l(itte)ra. [...] sp(ecie)s
v.b04 dicu(n)t aliq(ui)d[?] [...] naturam seu esse(n)tia(m) que
v.b05 indica(tur) p(er) g(e)n(u)s (et) d(iffe)r(enti)am si(n)e addito ex(tri)nseco

The adverb before sunt and the doubled q abbreviation in v.b01 are uncertain; the manuscript's compressed sign has not been regularized to a securely read quod quid erat esse. The numbered conclusion and solis speciebus specialissimis wording are visible. No exact parallel for this conclusion was established in Aquinas lectio 4. Paragraphs 6–7 there concern analogy; the old attribution of this specific conclusion to those paragraphs is withdrawn.

Source adjudication: Corpus Thomisticum, Sententia libri Metaphysicae VII, lectio 4 nn.3–4, [82899]–[82900], https://www.corpusthomisticum.org/cmp07.html. Digital Latin text based on Turin 1950 edition, not a facsimile of that print. Compared cached HTML and live page. Sustained wording and sequence from man/animal through whiteness/color, quale, substantiality, dependent entity, proportional similarity, and animal/color/number support a close textual relationship to Aquinas or a text transmitting this exposition. They do not establish direct copying or the compiler's identity. Shared Aristotelian examples alone would not suffice.

Significant departures: manuscript si queratur versus Aquinas cum enim quaero; extra li before color; tamen non rather than non tamen; apparent potest dici versus est; repeated quid est in v.a1–2; a corollary framing and numbered third conclusion absent from the checked Aquinas sequence. The compiler/work remains unidentified. Recommended Partial / medium confidence for source connection, not authorship.

Actual scope and inputs: manuscript r_full.jpg; z/ra1.jpg, z/ra5.jpg, z/ra6.jpg, z/ra7.jpg, z/rb2.jpg, z/rb5.jpg, z/rb6.jpg, z/rb7.jpg, z/va1.jpg, z/vb1.jpg, z/vb2.jpg; v/F-b8xt_c1_r0c1.jpg, all viewed at original detail. First record and k18-source.json read. No new enhancement. Additional passages are assisted checks, not independent corroborating readings. Much of the leaf remains untranslated and uncollated; no human palaeographic check.

Candidate research: a live Internet Archive item A336023 establishes an available digitization of Johannes Versor, Quaestiones in Aristotelis Metaphysicorum libros, Toulouse ca1482, Sevilla copy. Item metadata read at https://archive.org/details/A336023. Its linked OCR and PDF and alternative OCR endpoint failed to load; no page or textual passage from Versor was checked. A search result also located a Salamanca 1493 reproduction record via Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes, but the record open failed. These discoveries correct the old no-digitization claim without assigning or excluding Versor. Search queries for distinctive phrases did not add an identified compiling work. No conclusions about unprinted status, school, date, or locality follow from no-hits.
